site.title: Ariadne Lit
site.subtitle: A Guide through the Literature Labyrinth
site.description: Interactive explorer for research artifacts coded from Business Process Management (BPM) conference papers.

labels.stepsHint: Click a type to filter papers
labels.landscapeDescription: Papers by publication year and track. Hover for details, click to open.
labels.graphDescription: Explore connections between papers based on shared keywords and types of artifact.

typesOfInquiry.label: Formal Science
typesOfInquiry.description: Formal/mathematical inquiry: proofs, formalisms, and analytical models.

typesOfInquiry.label: Information Systems Engineering
typesOfInquiry.description: Design-science and engineering contributions such as frameworks, tools, and prototypes.

typesOfInquiry.label: Scientific Study
typesOfInquiry.description: Empirical studies that test hypotheses or theories.

typesOfInquiry.label: Inductive Study
typesOfInquiry.description: Exploratory, theory-building research grounded in observation.

typesOfInquiry.label: Meta-analysis
typesOfInquiry.description: Literature reviews and syntheses of existing research.

typesOfInquiry.label: Case Study Application
typesOfInquiry.description: Applied work reporting on real-world industrial deployments.

typesOfArtifact.label: Technique
typesOfArtifact.description: A specific procedure applied within a broader method.

typesOfArtifact.label: Method
typesOfArtifact.description: A structured, repeatable way of achieving a research or engineering goal.

typesOfArtifact.label: Software Product
typesOfArtifact.description: An implemented tool or system used to demonstrate feasibility.

typesOfArtifact.label: Conceptual Framework
typesOfArtifact.description: A structuring set of concepts, practices, or components.

typesOfArtifact.label: Model
typesOfArtifact.description: An abstract representation of a system, process, or phenomenon.

typesOfArtifact.label: Language
typesOfArtifact.description: A notation, modeling language, or formal language.

typesOfArtifact.label: Design Concept
typesOfArtifact.description: An idea or principle intended to guide design.

typesOfArtifact.label: Experience Report
typesOfArtifact.description: A descriptive account of findings, an application, or a case.

typesOfArtifact.label: Taxonomy
typesOfArtifact.description: A classification scheme organizing concepts or artifacts.

about.title: About This Project
about.introduction: Ariadne Lit shows what Business Process Management (BPM) research contributes and how it is done. Each paper from the BPM conference proceedings was coded by hand: which artifacts it contributes, which research and evaluation methods it uses, what data it relies on, whether an implementation is available, and which threats to validity it discusses. Browse the papers, see how they relate, and analyse patterns and trends across the field.

pages.description: Browse and search the papers, group them by any coded dimension, and see them on the Publication Timeline.
See how papers connect through shared keywords and similar artifacts, clustered by type of artifact.
Find which codes occur together and how practices change over time, with statistical tests.

dimensions.description: What the paper contributes, for example an algorithm, a method or a model. Coded for each paper.
How the artifact was developed, for example formal modelling or design science research.
How the artifact was evaluated, for example a benchmark, a case study or an illustrative example.
The kind of data used: real-world, synthetic, or mathematical formulae.
Whether an implementation exists and whether it is publicly available.
Which threats to validity the paper discusses, such as external or construct validity.
The kind of research the paper does as a whole, for example information systems engineering or a scientific study.
The kind of theory the paper builds on: formal or social science theory.
Whether the paper mainly contributes theory, an artifact, or both.

method.title: Data Source
method.content: Papers from the BPM conference proceedings, coded manually against the research-artifact coding scheme described above.

method.title: Coding Process
method.content: Active BPM researchers coded the papers over two years against a fixed coding scheme: two coders coded each paper independently, disagreements were resolved by consensus, and a third coder settled any that remained. This is part of a work soon under review.

method.title: Anonymization
method.content: Only a public sample of papers is shown with title, authors, keywords and DOI. All other papers are anonymized: their coded data still counts in every chart and statistic, but they are not listed and cannot be opened. Free-text summaries are removed from all papers.

method.title: Statistics
method.content: The Patterns & Trends page uses Fisher's exact test for pairs of codes that occur together, the Cochran–Armitage test for trends over time, and the Benjamini–Hochberg or Holm correction when many tests are run at once. Each view's "How to read this" explains the details.

about.addingPapers: To import a collection from a reference manager such as Zotero, export your library as a BibTeX (.bib) file, or create a bibliography in a supported citation style (APA, MLA, IEEE or Springer LNCS) and copy it to the clipboard. Either works as input for "+ Add Paper": drop the .bib file or paste the bibliography. Exporting the paper files (PDFs) is not necessary. Title, authors, year, DOI and conference are filled in for you; you then code each paper before it is added.
about.contribute: Missing a paper? Use "+ Add Paper" on Overview. Added papers are stored only in your browser; you can propose them for the shared dataset from there.
